findings.explanation: The SPL never reads `_internal` or metrics.log. It runs `| tstats count WHERE index=* by _time span=15m, sourcetype` over the indexed events of every non-internal index the searching role can see.
findings.suggested_fix: Say the data source is the index-time metadata (tsidx) of all production indexes, queried with `tstats` by sourcetype. No extra ingestion is needed. Optionally mention `metrics.log group=per_sourcetype_thruput` as an alternative feed.

findings.explanation: This search references no data model. `tstats` over `index=*` with `sourcetype` and `_time` reads index-time fields straight from tsidx files, so no acceleration is needed. Following this step sends the reader looking for a non-existent data model.
findings.quote: Uses `tstats` against precomputed summaries; ensure the referenced data model is accelerated.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with: '`tstats` reads index-time metadata (index, sourcetype, host, source, _time) directly from tsidx files. No data model acceleration is required.'

findings.explanation: `implementation` describes a train-weekly, apply-every-15-minutes design. The SPL runs `fit DensityFunction ... into sourcetype_volume_model`, so every scheduled run retrains the model on whatever time range that run covers and overwrites it. There is no separate `apply` search.
findings.quote: Schedule every 15 minutes against a 30-day trained DensityFunction model per sourcetype. ... Retrain the model weekly via a separate scheduled search.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the two-search pattern explicitly. (1) A weekly training search over 30 days using `fit DensityFunction count by sourcetype into sourcetype_volume_model`. (2) A 15-minute detection search over recent buckets using `apply sourcetype_volume_model`. Make clear that the SPL shown is the training form.

findings.explanation: The search counts events per sourcetype only. It has no error-rate measure and no per-forwarder grain, so it cannot detect an error-rate spike or say which forwarder stopped. `implementation` also promises enrichment with forwarder host metadata that the search does not perform.
findings.quote: Silent data pipeline breaks — a forwarder stops sending, a sourcetype drops to zero, or error rates spike
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the claim to per-sourcetype volume anomalies and zero-count gaps. If error rate is wanted, describe a companion search (for example a count of `log_level=ERROR` or HTTP 5xx per sourcetype). Describe host-level attribution as a follow-up drilldown by `host`.

findings.explanation: Placeholder text (`target_index`, `configured_sourcetype`) that misses this search's real false positives. Sparse or batch sourcetypes that legitimately log once an hour or once a day produce `count=0` (silent_drop) in most 15-minute buckets. The current, still-filling bucket at the end of the window reads low. Weekends and holidays dip below a model trained mostly on weekdays. A sourcetype that is completely silent for the whole window never appears at all, so a true total outage is missed rather than flagged.
findings.quote: Planned work for 'Log Volume and Error Rate Anomaly per Sourcetype (MLTK)' shifts `count` over `span=15m`
findings.suggested_fix: List those causes. Suggest an allow-list lookup of expected-cadence sourcetypes, ending the search at `latest=-15m@m` or similar so the incomplete bucket is excluded, and a separate expected-sourcetype inventory check for sourcetypes that have disappeared completely.

findings.explanation: The toolkit is listed on Splunkbase as app 2890, now titled 'Splunk AI Toolkit'. It requires the Python for Scientific Computing add-on for the search head's platform (for example Splunkbase 2882 for Linux 64-bit). The UC names neither.
findings.suggested_fix: List 'Splunk AI Toolkit (formerly MLTK, Splunkbase 2890)' plus 'Python for Scientific Computing (Splunkbase 2882 Linux / 2883 Windows)' as search-head prerequisites.

findings.explanation: This is generic platform-health text. It does not say the UC learns how much data each kind of log normally sends and flags a source that suddenly goes quiet or floods.
findings.quote: We watch platform health and capacity for search, indexing, and data delivery so the system we use for answers does not go dark or slow first.
findings.suggested_fix: For example: 'We learn how much data each kind of log usually sends every 15 minutes and raise a flag when one suddenly goes quiet or sends far more or less than normal, so we notice broken data feeds quickly.'

findings.explanation: An advanced-difficulty MLTK model with train/apply scheduling is placed in the crawl wave, which is meant for first-step detections.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it to walk or run, or add the basic volume and inventory UCs (for example UC-13.1.13) as prerequisites.

findings.explanation: PagerDuty is only an optional alert destination. It is not equipment that generates the monitored data.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The title promises 'Error Rate' anomaly detection, but the SPL models only event count per sourcetype.

The search uses `fit ... into` on every run instead of `apply`, so the model is retrained on each scheduled window. The final 15-minute bucket is incomplete when `latest=now`. Sourcetypes absent for the entire window are never zero-filled, so a total outage is missed.

summary: The SPL is a reasonable per-sourcetype volume model built on `tstats`, but the prose describes data sources (metrics.log), an error-rate signal and a train/apply schedule that the search does not use. The description, controlTest and knownFalsePositives still contain `target_index` and `configured sourcetype` placeholders.
